Senator Wayne Harper, a Republican from Taylorsville, sponsored legislation to eliminate Utah's taxation of Social Security benefits. The bill, designated SB0071, would remove Utah from a group of nine states that still tax these retirement payments. Harper articulated his position on the double-taxation issue during committee proceedings: "It is taxable dollars that's put in there. And then when it comes out, we're taxing it again." The Revenue and Taxation Committee voted 4-2 to advance Harper's proposal to the full Senate.

His efforts over the past two decades to drastically reduce income tax rates and rid Utah of tiered income taxes has meant less overall funding for our public education system and a higher reliance on lower income Utahns to pay taxes. When Harper entered office, Utah's education funding effort at a percent of personal income stood at 5.7%. Now, it's at 3.7% and we have the lowest education funding per pupil in the nation.

Wayne Harper, R-Taylorsville, was among 10 senators who voted to replace Proposition 3 with SB96. SB96 would allow individuals earning up to 100 percent of the federal poverty line to enroll in Medicaid, compared with 138 percent for Prop 3, and Utah would initially pay 30 percent of the Medicaid costs for new enrollees under SB96, a cost share three times larger than what the state would face under the voter-approved initiative. Harper represents District 6 in Taylorsville, where the proposition was supported by 55.5 percent of voters.

Harper has sponsored multiple bills increasing fees on electric vehicles, including: SB136 (2018): Added up to $120 annual registration fee on clean air vehicles. HB209 (2021): Proposed increasing EV fees to $300 annually (did not pass). HB301 (2023): Imposed 12.5% tax on electricity at EV charging stations. Environmental advocates have criticized these measures, arguing they 'slow electric vehicle adoption and promote poorer air quality.'

In 2023 Harper sponsored HB301, which passed, and will levy a tax of 12.5% on electricity at EV charging stations. This adds a third tax at charging stations in Utah on top of existing sales and franchise taxes, and some analyses estimate some EV owners will pay twice as much tax as gasoline fueled vehicle drivers.

S.B. 170 Election Schedule Amendments fulfills requests from leaders of the Utah Republican Party, the Utah Democratic Party and county clerks to eliminate confusion and facilitate a more clear and transparent election process. Senator Wayne Harper noted: "The current filing period has created uncertainty in regard to who's running for office on caucus night." He emphasized that this adjustment enables voters to make informed decisions during caucus meetings.

HB 410: Child Care Amendments was sponsored by Rep. Tracy Miller and Sen. Wayne Harper. This bill counts preschool teaching in child care as equivalent to school teaching for educator licensing and allows local governments to use up to 1% of housing and transit reinvestment zone funds to expand child care facilities. This bill passed the House Committee and House unanimously, passed the Senate Committee with a 2-1 vote, and passed the Senate unanimously.
